newsitem.title: USA: Madonna wins Golden Globe for best musical actress.
newsitem.headline: Madonna wins Golden Globe for best musical actress.

text.p: Madonna, the controversial pop star and actress, was named best actress in a musical or comedy film at Sunday night's Golden Globe Awards for her title role in "Evita".

"I have been so incredibly blessed this last year. I have so much to be thankful for," Madonna told the star-studded audience at the Beverly Hilton hotel, referring to the birth of her baby and her role as Argentina's Eva Peron.
Backstage, the blonde singer and dancer said "Evita" was "a great opportunity to challenge myself in my music, singing and dancing. I hope to keep going as an artist and keep making movies."

The best director for a motion picture award went to Milos Forman for "The People vs. Larry Flynt", the life story of the controversial publisher of "Hustler" magazine, starring Woody Harrelson in the title role.
Tom Cruise took the Golden Globe for best actor in a musical or comedy movie for his role in "Jerry Maguire."

Veteran performer Lauren Bacall won the Golden Globe for best performance by a supporting actress in a motion picture for her role in "The Mirror Has Two Faces." The best supporting actor's award for film went to Edward Norton for his part in "Primal Fear."

The 54th annual Golden Globe Awards, presented by the Hollywood Foreign Press Association and seen as a barometer of who may go on to win the coveted Academy Awards, also honoured Dustin Hoffman with the Cecil B. DeMille Award for his achievements.
"Dustin Hoffman has had a career filled with landmark achievements," Cruise said in a tribute to Hoffman.

In other early awards, John Lithgow won for best performance by an actor in a musical or comedy TV series for "3rd Rock From The Sun," while Helen Hunt won the equivalent actress award for "Mad About You."
"3rd Rock From The Sun" also won the Golden Globe for best musical or comedy television series.

Unlike the Academy Awards, which will be presented by the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences in March, the Golden Globes for the most part separate their honours between music and comedy films and television series and dramatic films and TV programmes.

British actress Helen Mirren won the best actress award for a mini-series or motion picture made for television for her role in "Losing Chase." Alan Rickman won the best actor award in the same category for "Rasputin."
